items.title: Goldeneyes sign Knowles, Messier to one-year contracts
items.summary: Vancouver invited Knowles to training camp while Messier was taken in the sixth round of the 2026 PWHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Courtesy of Vancouver Goldeneyes The Vancouver Goldeneyes added youth to their blue line Saturday, signing defenders Olivia Knowles and Ashley Messier to one-year contracts. The Goldeneyes invited Knowles to training camp while Messier was taken in the sixth round of the 2026 PWHL Draft. Knowles spent a season with the PHF’s Minnesota Whitecaps before she joined the Toronto Sceptres ahead of the PWHL’s inaugural season. She spent the next two seasons with the New York Sirens. She has one assist in 35 career PWHL games. Before she turned professional, the Campbell River, B.C., native spent five years at the University of Minnesota, where she served as co-captain in her fifth season. She recorded 17 goals and 61 assists for 78 points in 168 career NCAA games. Meanwhile, Messier spent five seasons playing college hockey, four at Cornell University and one at the University of Minnesota-Duluth. The native of Wilcox, Sask., scored 14 goals and added 44 assists for 58 points in 144 career NCAA games. The upcoming 2026-27 campaign will be the Goldeneyes’ second in the league. During their inaugural season, the team went 9-3-4-14 and finished with 37 points, seven points shy of the fourth and final playoff spots. Defender Sophie Jaques led the team in points with 20 and was tied with forwards Jenn Gardiner and Sarah Nurse for the most goals with nine. Emerance Maschmeyer and Kristen Campbell split the crease in 2025-26. Maschmeyer went 7-9-2 with a .916 save percentage (SV%) and 2.57 goals against average (GAA) in 19 games, while Campbell posted a mark of 5-5-2 with a .913 SV% and 2.17 GAA in 13 appearances.

items.title: Bruins’ David Pastrnak out against Canucks, listed as day-to-day
items.body: The Boston Bruins forward won't play Sunday against the Vancouver Canucks (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 5 p.m. ET / 3 p.m. PCT) after sustaining a lower-body injury, head coach Marco Sturm said Saturday. Pastrnak is being listed as day-to-day and will be reassessed Monday per Sturm. Pastrnak left Friday's 3-1 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs with a non-contact injury with six minutes left in the first. The Bruins captain leads the team in goals (11), assists (21) and points (32). Durability has been a hallmark of Pastrnak’s career. He missed five games last season, but played in all 82 in each of the previous three seasons. However, the Bruins could be getting another forward back in the form of rookie James Hagens , who has not played since Nov. 5 due to a back injury. The 20-year-old had been off to a fast start in his first full season with six goals and six assists in 17 games prior to going down. After facing the Canucks Sunday, the Bruins will host the Colorado Avalanche Tuesday before three days off.

items.title: Kraken Place Philipp Grubauer On IR, Recall Nikke Kokko
items.summary: The Seattle Kraken have placed goaltender Philipp Grubauer on IR and recalled Nikke Kokko from AHL Coachella Valley.
items.body: Register Login Kraken Place Philipp Grubauer On IR, Recall Nikke Kokko By Brian La Rose | at November 28, 2026 1:58 pm Kraken goaltender Philipp Grubauer was injured last night against Edmonton following a collision with Colton Dach . While he stayed in the game for a bit, he eventually left and did not return. The veteran is now set to miss the next week at a minimum, after the team announced ( Twitter link ) that Grubauer has been placed on injured reserve, which carries a minimum of a seven-day absence. In a corresponding move, netminder Nikke Kokko has been recalled on an emergency basis from AHL Coachella Valley. Grubauer is in the final season of a six-year, $35.4MM contract signed back in 2021, a deal that hasn’t gone particularly well for the most part. That said, his performance last season (2.65 GAA, .909 SV% in 32 games) was his best, although his numbers are more around the league average this year, checking in at 3.02 and .894, respectively, in 15 appearances. He has done enough to rebuild some of his value but he’ll still be facing a notable cut in pay in his next trip through free agency this summer. As for Kokko, he has been Seattle’s third-string option over the last couple of years, most recently serving as their extra goalie for their Global Series games earlier this month. The 22-year-old has a 2.99 GAA and an .897 SV% in a dozen outings with the Firebirds this season. Kokko has four career NHL appearances under his belt, three of which came last season when he turned aside 73 of 82 shots. He’s set to be a restricted free agent this summer.

items.title: Charge sign Jordan Ray, Tory Mariano to one-year contracts
items.summary: The Charge now have 21 players signed for the 2026-27 season and can sign three more under expanded roster rules.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL The Ottawa Charge are putting the finishing touches on their 2026-27 roster for the upcoming PWHL season, signing forward Jordan Ray and defender Tory Mariano on Saturday, a week before beginning their fourth regular-season campaign. Both have put pen to paper on one-year standard player agreements, bringing two of the Charge’s recent 2026 PWHL Draft picks into the picture officially after training camp. Ray, selected 23rd overall, and Mariano, 47th, will now begin their first professional seasons after impressive NCAA careers. Ray joins the Charge after leading the Yale University Bulldogs with a career-high 17 goals and 49 points in 36 games last season, including three four-point nights and a 14-game point streak. A native of Rockledge, Florida, the 22-year-old became the first player from the state to be drafted into the PWHL and is now the first from the state to sign a contract in the league. “After the first practice, I was like, ‘this is a lot different than college.’ I was like, ‘this is a lot faster pace, harder passes and everything.’ So after four days though, I feel like you get used to it,” Ray told reporters after making her pre-season debut for the Charge in a 2-1 win over the Detroit Clitch. “It’s just the first couple of drills with, like, the nerves too and get them all out, and it’s been good.” While the league will play its first pair of PWHL Takeover Tour games in the Sunshine State this season, Ray won’t get the chance to participate, as the Charge were not selected for those showcase events. Inside the locker room after the game, Beauvillier’s hospital bracelet was spotted once again during Spencer Carbery’s post-game victory speech. Sitting beside Boone Jenner , Beauvillier held up the penalty-killing’s arm as Carbery praised his teammate’s shot-blocking heroics earlier in the night. With a point, a Capitals win, and a healthy baby boy, Beauvillier had plenty to be thankful for this Thanksgiving. items.title: Canucks Place Elias Pettersson On IR, Recall Chase Wouters
items.summary: The Vancouver Canucks have placed center Elias Pettersson on injured reserve and recalled forward Chase Wouters from AHL Abbotsford.
items.body: Register Login Canucks Place Elias Pettersson On IR, Recall Chase Wouters By Brian La Rose | at November 28, 2026 12:58 pm The Canucks have made a pair of roster moves in advance of their game on Sunday against Boston. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve placed center Elias Pettersson on injured reserve. Taking his place on the roster is forward Chase Wouters , who has been recalled from AHL Abbotsford. Pettersson has been sidelined since sustaining an upper-body injury on November 19th against Seattle. Vancouver’s announcement indicated that they’ve backdated the IR placement to that date, meaning he has already served the minimum seven days. Accordingly, Pettersson will be eligible to be activated as soon as he gets the green light to return, though that clearly won’t be coming this weekend. It has been a nice bounce-back year for the 28-year-old, who has been a bright spot on a Canucks team that has struggled mightily this season. Pettersson sits second on the team in scoring with six goals and 17 assists in 23 games, his highest point-per-game average since the 2023-24 campaign. While that’s still not the type of production expected from a top center with a $11.6MM cap hit, it’s still a definite step in the right direction in the first season under new head coach Manny Malhotra. As for Wouters, this is his first career recall, although it’s his sixth season in Vancouver’s system. The 26-year-old went undrafted and after his junior career with WHL Saskatoon ended in 2020, he inked a minor-league pact with Vancouver’s farm team in Abbotsford. items.summary: Rakell and Rust are both 30-goal scorers and each have reached the 60-point mark twice.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: USA TODAY Sports The Pittsburgh Penguins have struggled so far in 2026-27, losing 10 of their last 13 games and sitting near the bottom of the NHL standings . There’s been plenty of scrutiny on the status of future Hockey Hall of Famers like Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin, and if they would be willing to be traded. Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas hasn’t shied away from wanting to start a proper rebuild, and moving veteran assets could kickstart that. However, two players who many teams are also looking at are forwards Rickard Rakell and Bryan Rust. items.body: Adam Fox and Brandon Montour are using the platform their NHL fame provides to bring awareness and fundraising to a personal cause that in a perfect world wouldn't exist at all. Fox, a New York Rangers defenseman, and Montour, a Seattle Kraken defenseman, know too well the impact of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, the currently incurable nervous system disease known as ALS. Fox's father-in-law is 62-year-old former NFL linebacker Tim Green, who has been living with ALS since 2016. Montour's brother, Cameron, died from the disease on Oct. 20, 2025, seven weeks shy of his 35th birthday, leaving behind wife, Chelsey, and daughters Peyton and Parker. Unified by their personal experiences, Fox and Montour are working with a coalition born out of ALS Action Canada called Courage to Fight ALS to bring awareness about the disease, to tell their personal stories associated with it, to raise money toward finding a cure, and to promote it across the NHL. "We're connected through this thing," Fox said. "It's not in a very pleasant way, but it's nice to have someone to try to build this with." Fox and Montour are of course quite busy with their regular jobs, but they are each giving much of their personal time toward the fight against ALS, also known as Lou Gehrig’s Disease. Since the start of last season, Fox, who wears No. 23, has been donating $1,023 for every goal he scores and $523 for every assist to Tackle ALS, the initiative that Green, who played eight seasons with the Atlanta Falcons, started jointly with the Sean M. items.body: Dedication, grit hallmarks of defenseman's 20-season NHL career The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel , T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior writer Dan Rosen profiles Suter. Ryan Suter 's reaction to getting into the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame is on brand for the former NHL defenseman. Gracious but humble. Never selfish, thinking only about the people that matter most to him and how they feel, how they would react. "People ask me and I'm just like, 'You know, it's cool, but it's more about my family,'" Suter said. "I wish my dad was here because that would be pretty cool for him. My Uncle Gary, my grandparents -- for me, yeah, it's cool, don't get me wrong, it's pretty awesome, but it's more about them." Suter will be inducted at a ceremony at the Grand Hyatt in Washington on Nov. 30. Joining him in the Class of 2026 are fellow Wisconsin natives Phil and Amanda Kessel, former Team USA teammate TJ Oshie, and Stan Wong, a longtime athletic trainer for USA Hockey. Bob Suter, Ryan's father, was inducted in 2003 as a member of 1980 USA "Miracle on Ice" team. The other ones to hit 60 this early were Wayne Gretzky, Bernie Nicholls, Mike Bossy and Phil Esposito. Edmonton looked to have gone up 3-1 with 23 seconds left in the second period as McDavid blasted the puck into the net on an odd-man rush. However, Draisaitl was given a penalty for interference on the play, a blown call as the replay revealed that Brandon Montour had tripped over his own discarded stick. Taking the ice on a line with Dylan Strome and Anthony Beauvillier , the 41-year-old forward played just 7:50, with 3:31 in the first period, 2:12 in the second, and 2:07 in the third. Notably, Ovechkin took the ice for just 33 seconds on the power play. He has no PPGs and just one power-play point this season. While Ovechkin didn’t see the ice much, his line-mates both got into double digits, with Strome getting 13:42 TOI and Beauvillier getting 10:40. Ovechkin was the only Capitals player not to see more than 10 minutes. Ovechkin’s 7:50 of ice time against the Panthers is 3:06 less than his previous career low — 10:56 in a game against the Nashville Predators on October 29. All 11 of Ovechkin’s lowest ice times of his career occurred this season — in a span of just 23 games. items.summary: Linus Ullmark stopped 18 shots, Michael Amadio had a goal and two assists and Tim Stutzle scored twice as the Ottawa Senators defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-2 on Friday.
items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Linus Ullmark stopped 18 shots, Michael Amadio had a goal and two assists and Tim Stutzle scored twice as the Ottawa Senators defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-2 on Friday. Ullmark has allowed two or fewer goals in 13 of his 15 starts and improved to 13-2 on the season to become the first goaltender in NHL history to win at least 13 of his first 15 games in a season multiple times. He also started 13-1 to begin the 2022-23 season with Boston when he won the Vezina Trophy. Jake Guentzel scored twice for the Lightning, which finished a six-game homestand 2-4 after starting the season with eight consecutive wins at home. Greig put the Senators up at 3:37 of the first period with a side-angle shot from the outside of the left circle. Stutzle finished off an Amadio pass for a shorthanded goal to make it 2-0 at 12:47. Amadio made it 3-0 at 6:20 of the second period while Stutzle grabbed a rebound on an odd-man rush to make it 4-0 at 17:37. Zub and Giroux scored 1:38 apart in the third before Guentzel scored twice in a span of 4:45. More importantly, though, Roberson was given a 10-game break following a match penalty for an “attempt to injure.” Roberson dragged Marentette down at the conclusion of the fight which resulted in Marentette getting put into a concussion protocol The OHL said Roberson “utilized an unacceptable tactic in a fighting situation” and that it was “a dangerous takedown move that involved using the leg as leverage.” Marentette, meanwhile, was given three games for a major kneeing penalty. The trade market for NHL goalies has shrunk considerably in the wake of the blockbuster Connor Hellebuyck trade from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils , but that doesn't mean there aren't still teams out there that are interested in upgrading in net. items.summary: The Canadiens will be without Kaiden Guhle against the Golden Knights, adding to their defensive challenges with Mike Matheson already sidelined. Meanwhile, Ivan Demidov inches closer to a return as Montreal looks to get its struggling power play back on track and clean up its execution.
items.body: LAS VEGAS— Any hope that Kaiden Guhle would be available to play against the Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday was erased when the Montreal Canadiens announced on Friday that the defenceman was day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Guhle left almost halfway through Wednesday’s 6-0 loss in Colorado, seconds after being hit from behind and knocked into the boards by Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog. He did not return. “It’s a tough loss, a tough guy to replace,” said Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki, who knew that the absence of Mike Matheson had already had its impact on the team’s recent skid. The Canadiens have lost three consecutive games in regulation for the first time since last November and the absence of their most used player—Matheson—has been an undeniable factor in that. Now, without both Matheson and Guhle, rookies Adam Engstrom and David Reinbacher will get more runway while Arber Xhekaj and Alex Carrier will need to be relied on almost as much as Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson typically are. The latter has struggled mightily this season, saying after Wednesday’s tough game in Denver, “Obviously it hasn’t been good enough at times, and that’s on me, I’ve got to find a way.” Dobson is Montreal’s highest-paid defenceman, a former 70-point producer who’s scored at least 10 goals in each of the last five seasons but is stuck on zero through 26 games of this one. But the Canadiens aren’t concerned about Dobson filling the opposing net. They need him to be stalwart in helping to keep goals out of theirs in the absence of their best defensive defenceman. items.title: Blackhawks place Patrick Kane on IR with lower-body injury
items.body: CHICAGO — The injury-depleted Chicago Blackhawks placed veteran forward Patrick Kane on injured reserve with a lower-body injury before Friday's game against the Rangers and recalled forward Landon Slaggert from Rockford of the AHL. Kane's move to the IR, retroactive to Wednesday, means the NHL's all-time leading American-born scorer will miss at least seven days. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said that in a “best-case scenario,” the 38-year-old might return at Nashville on Thursday. Chicago is already without star center Connor Bedard, sidelined for about four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery on Monday. Defenseman Bowen Byram is skating, but remains out with an upper-body injury and his return date remains unclear. He has played in just six games after being acquired from Buffalo in an offseason trade. Blashill said he didn't believe Kane, a nine-time All-Star in his 20th season and second tour with Chicago, would be out long term. But then he hedged. “But I don't want to say that without knowing for sure, but we didn't put him on the LTIR (long-term injured reserve),” Blashill said. “We anticipate this is something that can be managed and he could be back sooner than later.” Kane has two goals and 16 assists in 22 games this season. He returned to the Blackhawks, who drafted him first overall in 2007, in July after signing a two-year, $16 million contract. The 24-year-old Slaggert has four goals and six assists in 20 games for Rockford. He has played in 102 career NHL games with the Blackhawks over three seasons, recording six goals and 11 assists. items.title: Connor Brown’s third-period goal lifts Devils to comeback win over Flames
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Connor Brown scored the go-ahead goal off a scramble in front with 3:58 remaining to lead the New Jersey Devils to a come-from-behind 5-3 win over the Calgary Flames on Friday. After Brown’s eighth goal, New Jersey had to kill off a penalty to Jonas Siegenthaler with 2:22 to play to preserve the win. The Devils, who are 11-3 at home, had their NHL-leading 10th comeback victory. Luke Hughes scored twice, including an empty-netter with 11 seconds left, and Jack Hughes had a goal and three assists for a four-point game for the seventh time in his career for the Devils. Timo Meier also scored and Jake Allen stopped 26 shots. Matt Coronado, Zach Whitehead and Joel Hanley had goals for the Flames. Devin Cooley had 29 saves. Jack Hughes tied it at 3 as he was falling down near the crease at 12:25 of the third period on assists from Dougie Hamilton and Arseny Gritsyuk. The Flames erased a 2-1 deficit in the second period with goals from Coronato and Whitecloud to grab a 3-2 lead. New Jersey scored twice within 12 seconds at the start of the second period to go ahead 2-1. Luke Hughes scored his eighth goal of the season from Jack Hughes and Hamilton 56 seconds into the period, then Meier had a goal at 1:08. Calgary went up 1-0 on Hanley's second goal of the season in his 12th game. Yegor Sharangovich and Simon Nemec had the assists, with Nemec extending his points streak to a career-high six games. Nemec was traded to the Flames in June. He was drafted by the Devils with the second pick of the 2022 draft and skated in 155 games with New Jersey.

Sure enough he never did, ending his day after 5:50 as the B’s lost 3-1. In a video posted by the New England Sports Network, the Boston captain was seen rushing up ice only to be bothered and heading back to the bench after no contact occurred, limping down the tunnel to the dressing room. Always concerning when such an injury occurs without contact, the Czech has been one of the most durable stars across the league over the past several seasons. Missing just five regular season games since 2022-23, Pastrňák had a streak of three consecutive 82-game campaigns end one year ago with an undisclosed injury . Playing at his usual star level, Pastrňák has 11 goals and 32 points in 24 games this year. It is a continuation of last seasons’ 71-assist effort, an all-time high, continuing to showcase his evolution from a pure sniper to an elite playmaker who can drive offense like few others in the league. Currently ranked 11th in the NHL, speaking to the quality of their Atlantic Division where they find themselves fourth, the Bruins will hope Pastrňák is good to go by Sunday against the Canucks.

items.title: Leafs’ Chris Tanev leaves game against Bruins with injury
items.summary: Tanev was hurt after taking a hit from Boston’s Marc Kastelic during Friday’s game.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Tell me if you’ve heard this before. Chris Tanev is injured. During a Friday matinee matchup between the Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins , Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev suffered a lower-body injury that forced him to leave the game early. Early in the second period, Tanev went back behind his net to retrieve the puck. After delivering a breakout pass, he took a hit from Bruins forward Marc Kastelic. The check didn’t seem all that ferocious, but Kastelic caught Tanev in a soft spot down low, leaving Tanev in distress. Play came to a halt as Tanev needed assistance coming off the ice. He went down to the Leafs’ dressing room and didn’t return to the game. He logged just 7:53 of ice time across 11 shifts. The 36-year-old has seemingly been on the injured list as much as he has actually dressed for the Maple Leafs during his tenure with the Original Six franchise. He already missed nine games due to an upper-body injury back in October, which came after playing just 11 games for the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign. The injury comes just a few days after the Toronto native potted his first goal of the season, scoring in a 4-2 win over the New York Islanders on Tuesday night. The average NHL goalie has never been taller.
Goalies hit an average of 6-foot-3 for the first time in League history in 2024-25, and after the average dipped by one-tenth of an inch in 2025-26, are right back up to those lofty heights so far this season. That’s an increase
items.body: Statistical edge due in part to better adjustment against east-west offensive tactics Goalies hit an average of 6-foot-3 for the first time in League history in 2024-25, and after the average dipped by one-tenth of an inch in 2025-26, are right back up to those lofty heights so far this season. That’s an increase of 1.3 inches from 15 years ago, which probably isn’t a shock given the NHL push toward larger goalies who, in theory, take up more of the net. So, what has that rise meant for smaller goalies during the same period? Perhaps surprisingly, the number of goalies playing regularly at 6-foot-1 or shorter has remained somewhat steady during the same 15-year period. Already this season, 18 goalies listed at 6-foot-1 or shorter have appeared in at least one game, and 15 are playing a regular role, same as last season and one below the average across the previous four seasons. That list includes rookies Jacob Fowler of the Montreal Canadiens (6-1), Dylan Garand of the New York Rangers (6-1) and Devon Levi of the Edmonton Oilers (6-0). “Honestly, it's less of a conversation now than it used to be,” said Levi, adding size is not something he discusses with good friends and offseason training partners Garand and Jet Greaves of the Columbus Blue Jackets, a fellow 6-foot goalie. “The game has changed a lot in the past, I don't know, 10 years, and it continues to change, and there's so much more than just being big.” The gap between the number of games played by goalies 6-foot-1 or shorter and goalies 6-foot-5 or taller has shrunk significantly the past 15 years, from 856 games in 2011-12 to an average of 152.2 during the past five seasons, and smaller goalies had only played seven more games this season. items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Eric Cruikshank Partner Nov 27, 2026 7:05 PM Published Nov 27, 2026 7:05 PM The 21-year-old will be scratched after reportedly violating team rules. The Philadelphia Flyers' turbulent season just took another dark turn. The Flyers announced on Friday that Matvei Michkov will not be playing against the Vancouver Canucks due to an "internal team matter." Notably, this statement was made by Dan Hilferty, Flyers Governor and CEO of Comcast Spectacor, not GM Daniel Briere or president Keith Jones. This announcement came after Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman initially reported that Michkov had "violated team rules." Michkov's name has been circulating in the rumor mill after ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported on Nov. 10 that the 21-year-old would "likely want a new start elsewhere." Weekes added that he is a prime candidate moving forward. GM Daniel Briere has since come out and refuted any reports surrounding the possibility of Michkov being traded. Speaking with Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli earlier this month, Briere said he did not not receive a request for a trade from Michkov's agent, and that the organization was surprised by Weekes' reporting. Michkov is in the final year of his entry-level contract and is set to become a restricted free agent at the conclusion of the 2026-27 season. The Russian winger leads the Flyers with 11 goals and 20 points in 27 games. Michkov was selected seventh overall by the Flyers in 2023 and has posted 134 points in 188 career games. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Some roster management for the team in Orange County, as it trudges through the start of the holiday season without one of its star players. According to the NHL Media Site, the Anaheim Ducks have placed forward Leo Carlsson on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Carlsson has been out of action since last Saturday, when he was hurt during a game against the Utah Mammoth . During that contest, Carlsson was attempting to get the puck into the offensive zone. He was met with a firm check from Mammoth defenseman Mikhail Sergachev, which led to the two colliding with a linesman at the Utah blue line. Carlsson sat on the ice for a few minutes, with his hands to his face, before being helped off the ice by the Ducks’ training staff. Anaheim went on to lose to the Mammoth, 3-2. The young Swede has already missed the past two contests, which saw the Ducks lose to the Seattle Kraken , before hammering the San Jose Sharks 7-0 on Wednesday night. With Carlsson’s placement on IR retroactive to Nov. 21, he will be forced to miss Anaheim’s home-and-home against the rival Los Angeles Kings , but will be eligible to return to the lineup next Tuesday, when the Ducks welcome the Minnesota Wild to town. After signing his massive new deal prior to the start of the 2026-27 season, the 21-year-old has been a key part of Anaheim’s success in the early going. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Flyers have announced that forward Matvei Michkov will not play Friday against the Vancouver Canucks due to an “internal team matter.” The news was first reported by Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman and later confirmed by the Flyers. No specifics were given by the club. Michkov’s name has been the subject of trade rumors all season despite playing at a 62-point pace. Michkov has 11 goals and 20 points in 27 games, despite his ice time fluctuating all over the place. He was benched late in a 7-3 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday after taking a pair of minor penalties and finishing as a -2 with no points. Michkov has just one goal in the past 10 contests, but is still tracking for 34 on the season. The 21-year-old winger has 57 goals and 134 points in 188 career games with the Flyers since going seventh overall in 2023. The Perm, Russia native set a personal-best of 63 points as a rookie in 2024-25, but fell to 51 games last year as claims about his conditioning became a major talking point. The Flyers are currently fifth in the Eastern Conference wild-card race with a 9-12-6 record, giving them 24 points on the season. That’s five behind the New York Islanders for the final spot in the Metropolitan Division, and seven points behind the Florida Panthers in the wild-card race. The Flyers have a 5-3-2 record over the past 10 games, but have a real shot at getting back in the win column against the last-place Canucks.

items.title: Who players would pick to officiate an NHL game among their teammates
items.summary: The recent nationwide grounding in the U.S. opened up peculiar possibilities. As unorthodox as NHL players stepping in to officiate. It never got to that. But if it ever did, Sportsnet asked players which teammates they’d pick to serve as referees or linesmen.
items.body: Two weeks ago, the Federal Aviation Administration in the United States made a sudden decision to ground all planes, interrupting air travel across the country. This had the potential to throw the sports world into chaos too, as teams were making their way to their next locations. In the end, the schedule carried on as normal for the NHL. There were no game postponements and everyone got to where they needed to be. The NFL's games went on as planned too, but there was at least one element affected when officiating assignments had to be overhauled. Four NFL refs had to officiate two games on the same day. Starting with an afternoon Dolphins-Colts game in Indianapolis, the refs then had to drive to Cincinnati to be ready for an 8:20 p.m. ET start time for the Steelers-Bengals game. In the end, the nationwide grounding lasted a little over four hours and the sports world was not affected on a greater scale. But what if it went on longer and had a wider-ranging impact? What would happen if a group of NHL officials couldn't make it to an assigned game on time? This is covered in the NHL rulebook in rule 31.11, and opens up the possibility that players would have to officiate the game their teams are involved in: If, through misadventure or sickness, the Referees and Linespersons appointed are prevented from appearing, the League will make every attempt to find suitable replacement officials, otherwise, the Managers or Coaches of the two Clubs shall agree on Referee(s) and Linesperson(s). If they are unable to agree, they shall appoint a player from each side who shall act as Referee and Linesperson; the player of the home Club acting as Referee and the player of the visiting Club as Linesperson. items.title: Ukraine urges countries to follow Canada’s lead in barring Russian athletes
items.body: Ukraine's sports minister wants other countries to follow Canada's lead in blocking Russian teams from international hockey tournaments. Matviy Bidnyi, in an op-ed published Friday by the Ukrainian news agency RBC-Ukraine, credited diplomatic efforts by Ukrainian government officials for Canada's decision to bar Russian players from next month's world junior hockey championship in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Bidnyi said he is pushing for similar restrictions in other countries to prevent Russia's return to international hockey. Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier this month that Russian players would not be permitted to compete in Canada as long as Russia's war in Ukraine continues. The International Ice Hockey Federation announced Wednesday it would challenge a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling ordering the reinstatement of Russian teams to five international championships. Russia and Belarus have been barred from international hockey since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, and several European federations have vowed to boycott games if Russia is allowed to compete.

items.title: Flyers’ Matvei Michkov won’t play vs. Canucks after violating team rules
items.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers are keeping Matvei Michkov out of the lineup for Friday’s game against the Vancouver Canucks.
items.body: The Philadelphia Flyers are keeping Matvei Michkov out of the lineup for Friday's game against the Vancouver Canucks . Flyers governor Dan Hilferty announced that the decision to hold out Michkov was because of an internal matter. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Michkov was not playing because of a violation of team rules. The 21-year-old is in the midst of his third season with the Flyers, leading the team with 11 goals and 20 points in 27 games. Friedman reported back on Nov. 14 that both general manager Daniel Briere and president of hockey operations Keith Jones told Michkov the team had no interest in trading him. The Russian, who was the seventh overall pick in the 2023 draft, is in the final year of his three-year entry-level contract. "The other thing that I believe they did was they asked around with some of the younger players who are closer to Michkov's age about how they felt about him as well, and I think the feedback was positive," said Friedman. "So they are going to build this around Michkov and his young teammates. That is their goal here. They told him he was not in danger of being traded." Briere also echoed that notion when he spoke to Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli, saying of trade rumours , “This is all news to me. No, that’s not the plan at all. We’ve never discussed that.”

items.title: Devils’ Connor Hellebuyck to start vs. Jets on Saturday
items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck will get a chance to play against his former team.
items.body: Connor Hellebuyck will get a chance to play against his former team. The New Jersey Devils have confirmed that Hellebuyck will start Saturday's game against the Winnipeg Jets (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. CT). This will be the first time Hellebuyck faces his former team since he was traded to the Devils in October, following a contentious ending to his 11-year tenure with the Jets. He will not suit up for Friday's game against the Calgary Flames, with Jake Allen getting the start and David Rittich getting recalled to serve as the backup. Hellebuyck demanded a trade over the summer and was suspended by the Jets after failing to report to training camp. The 33-year-old netminder didn't play against the Jets when the Devils visited Winnipeg on Nov. 10, with management saying it was their decision to have him sit. Hellebuyck has a 9-1-1 record with the Devils and began his tenure with the team on a 7-0-0 run before a 3-2 defeat to the Montreal Canadiens in mid-November. During his time with the Jets, Hellebuyck was a four-time all-star and three-time Vezina winner.

items.title: Palmieri expected out rest of season for Islanders with torn right ACL, meniscus
items.summary: Kyle Palmieri is expected to be out for the rest of the regular season for the New York Islanders because of a torn right ACL and meniscus.
items.body: Forward was limited to 25 games after tearing left ACL last season Kyle Palmieri is expected to be out for the rest of the regular season for the New York Islanders because of a torn right ACL and meniscus. The 35-year-old forward was injured in a collision with Toronto Maple Leafs forward Easton Cowan during the second period of a 4-2 loss Monday. The Islanders, who gave a 6-8 month recovery time, placed Palmieri on injured reserve Tuesday. "I have spoken to him," Islanders coach Peter DeBoer said. "You know what? Again, it's emotional, and it's really raw right now. There's nothing you can say. I think he just wants to be out there with us. He wants to be in the battle. He likes this group and what was going on, and it's heartbreaking that he can't be a part of it." Palmieri has nine points (four goals, five assists) in 23 games this season. This marks the second straight season Palmieri sustained a significant knee injury, almost a year to the day after he tore the ACL in his left knee in a collision with Philadelphia Flyers defenseman Jamie Drysdale on Nov. 28, 2025. "I think I used the word 'heartbreaking.' It's emotional," DeBoer said. "People don't see the work that he put in to come back from what he went through last year in order to get to the point he got to this year. And then to have it happen like that to the other leg in such a fluky kind of thing, it's heartbreaking, emotional, all those words. So, he's out for the regular season, and we'll see after that." Palmieri was limited to 25 games last season, but was able to return for the Islanders' regular-season opener this season. items.title: Maple Leafs’ Dakota Joshua scratched vs. Bruins due to illness
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs are being forced to make a depth adjustment. Fourth-line forward Dakota Joshua has been ruled out for Friday's matchup against the Boston Bruins due to an illness, the team announced . According to Sportsnet's Luke Fox , Zack MacEwen , who was meant to be a healthy scratch, will slot into Joshua's spot. Joshua, 30, is in his second season with the Maple Leafs and has logged two goals and an assist through 11 appearances. His second marker of the year came in Toronto's skid-busting 4-2 win over the New York Islanders on Monday. He's one point shy of reaching the 100-point plateau for his career, currently sitting at 52 goals and 47 assists through 307 regular-season games. As for MacEwen, Friday's tilt will be his 21st appearance of the season, scoring three goals and three assists thus far. He's currently riding a five-game pointless streak, last ticking the box score with a goal and assist in the Maple Leafs' 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Nov. 12. items.title: Islanders’ Kyle Palmieri out 6-8 months with torn ACL
items.summary: Palmieri suffered a torn ACL on his other knee nearly one year ago to the day, which forced him to miss the rest of 2025-26.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brad Penner The New York Islanders announced Friday that forward Kyle Palmieri will be out six-to-eight months with a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee. The team placed the winger on injured reserve earlier this week after he suffered what they termed as a lower-body injury against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday. It’s the same injury that Palmieri, 35, suffered almost one year ago to the day that forced him to miss the final 57 games of the 2025-26 regular season. If he misses the rest of the current season, he will have only played 48 games since the end of the 2024-25 campaign. Palmieri had four goals and five assists for nine points in 23 games this season. Through 17 NHL seasons, the 2009 first-round pick has 280 goals and 274 assists for 554 points in 948 regular-season games with the Islanders, New Jersey Devils and Anaheim Ducks . He’s twice hit the 30-goal mark and has recorded at least 50 points four times, which includes a career-high 57 in 2015-16 with the Devils. He’s also appeared in 68 career Stanley Cup Playoff games, where he’s recorded 18 goals and 14 assists for 32 points. He was part of the Ducks’ and Islanders’ conference final runs in 2015 and 2021, respectively. Palmieri, born in Smithtown, N.Y., and raised in New Jersey, spent parts of four seasons in the American Hockey League. He scored 75 goals and added 59 assists for 134 points in 148 career games. The Islanders go into Friday with a 12-7-5 record and 29 points , which puts them third in the Metropolitan Division .

items.body: The veteran winger has suffered a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee and will be out for six to eight months, the New York Islanders announced on Friday. Palmieri's injury occurred during Monday's loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs, when he sustained a lower-body injury after getting tangled with Leafs players near the net and taking an awkward fall toward the goal. He was placed on injured reserve the next day. It marks the second consecutive season the 35-year-old's campaign has been cut short due to a major lower-body injury. He suffered a torn ACL in his left knee almost exactly a year ago and wound up missing the rest of the 2025-26 season after starting strong, with 18 points (six goals, 12 assists) through 25 appearances. Palmieri had logged four goals and five assists through 23 games in 2026-27 prior to his latest setback. His latest string of injury misfortune comes after the 17-year vet had built up a reputation as one of the game's more durable players — playing in at least 50 regular-season games in 12 of those seasons, including a streak of 223 consecutive appearances for the Islanders prior to his injury last year. Palmieri was a first-round pick by the Anaheim Ducks in 2009. He has 280 goals and 274 assists in 948 regular-season games with the Ducks, Devils and Islanders.

items.summary:
Jeff Petry announced his retirement from the NHL after 16 seasons on Thursday.
The 38-year-old defenseman had nine assists in 67 games with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild last season. He did not have a point in three Stanley Cup Playoff games.
items.body: Defenseman played 1,048 games, including for Panthers, Wild last season Jeff Petry announced his retirement from the NHL after 16 seasons on Thursday. The 38-year-old defenseman had nine assists in 67 games with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild last season. He did not have a point in three Stanley Cup Playoff games. Petry made the announcement on his wife's podcast "Never Offside with Julie & Cat." Selected by the Edmonton Oilers in the second round (No. 45) of the 2006 NHL Draft, Petry had 394 points (96 goals, 298 assists) in 1,048 regular-season games for the Edmonton Oilers, Montreal Canadiens, Pittsburgh Penguins, Detroit Red Wings, Panthers and Wild. He had 13 points (five goals, eight assists) in 51 playoff games and made the Cup Final with the Canadiens in 2020-21 when they lost to the Tampa Bay Lightning in five games. Petry played in his 1,000th game while with the Panthers last season against the Vancouver Canucks on Nov. 17, 2025. "Playing 1,000 games going into last year, that was a goal of mine and to be able to accomplish that was great," he said. The Ann Arbor native, who got to play for his hometown Red Wings for two seasons from 2023-25, also discussed some of his favorite NHL memories. "My first (NHL) game in Edmonton (Dec. 28, 2010)," Petry said. "That dream finally came true. Scoring my first goal (Jan. 20, 2011). The biggest memory was playing in the finals with Montreal. Obviously not the ending result (we wanted), but to be able to do that was special." Petry also represented the United States at the IIHF World Championships four times (2012-2014, 2024), including winning the bronze medal in 2013. items.title: Kessel’s love of playing in NHL led to U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame
items.summary: The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, T.J. Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel.
items.body: 3-time Cup champ holds ironman streak with 1,064 straight regular-season games The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel , T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel. Phil Kessel played through the pain, the bumps, the bruises and all those mornings when he arrived at the rink just not feeling right. He’d play 1,064 consecutive regular-season games, in fact, an NHL Ironman record built over nearly 13 years and five teams. He played through injuries others never knew about, the pressure of being a star and three long Stanley Cup Playoffs runs. Kessel never set out to chase the record. In an interview with NHL Network Radio and during his election press conference, he said he simply hated sitting out. "I don't think it was ever a priority," Kessel said. "I just always wanted to play in the games. I love playing the games. I love playing hockey and I never wanted to miss. "As a player and competitor, you never want to sit out. You never want to be in the stands. You never want to be injured. You always want to be out there." That passion, durability and understated competitiveness helped make Kessel one of the most accomplished American players of his generation. Now, the reluctant superstar and three-time Stanley Cup champion is headed to the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame. Kessel and his sister, Amanda, an Olympic gold medalist and four-time IIHF Women's World Championship gold medalist, headline the Class of 2026 to be inducted at the dinner and ceremony at the Grand Hyatt Washington in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 30. The Madison, Wisconsin, natives will become the second sister-brother combination inducted, joining Cammi Granato and Tony Granato.

items.body: Register Login Brenden Dillon Receives Four-Game Suspension By Brian La Rose | at November 26, 2026 6:00 pm With the Devils having an early afternoon game on Friday, the Department of Player Safety was going to have to make a quick ruling on the fate of Brenden Dillon after his hearing today. They did just that, announcing that the defenseman has received a four-game suspension for his hit on Columbus blueliner Denton Mateychuk . In the video accompanying the announcement, it was noted that Dillon was deemed to have elevated “upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk’s head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable” . Because it was deemed avoidable, it became grounds for suspension under Rule 48. Meanwhile, he received a match penalty for the hit, which occurred a little past the midway mark of the first period. It is the second suspension of the 36-year-old’s career, the other coming back in February 2024, also for an illegal check to the head. However, since more than two years had elapsed, he didn’t qualify as a repeat offender for the purpose of salary forfeiture, though the prior act could still be considered when determining the number of games of the suspension. Dillon will forfeit a little over $82K in salary, with that money going to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. Meanwhile, he’ll be eligible to return on December 5th against Pittsburgh.
